data.name: StatusIdle
data.value: > what do you want to do?

data.name: HintIdle
data.value: Share your music, or listen to a phone nearby.

data.name: HintStreaming
data.value: Play your music in any app: it is shared live.

data.name: HintSearching
data.value: The phones must be paired over Bluetooth and a few meters from each other.

data.name: HintListening
data.value: You hear their music live. You can turn the screen off.

data.name: TutorialWelcomeText
data.value: Your phone can now do something it never could: stream its music to the phones around you. No Wi-Fi, no internet.

data.name: TutorialPairText
data.value: Only once: on one phone, open Settings › Bluetooth › Pair new device, pick the other phone and confirm the code on both.

data.name: TutorialBroadcastText
data.value: Whoever has the music taps “Share my sound” and accepts the permissions. Android calls it “screen recording”: that is how it lets AuraMusic capture the sound, nothing is recorded. Then play your music, in any app.

data.name: TutorialListenText
data.value: The others tap “Listen”: their phone finds the broadcaster on its own and reconnects if you drift apart. The screen can be off.

data.name: TutorialTipsText
data.value: Stay within a few meters. The sound arrives slightly delayed: in the same room, everyone wears headphones to avoid echo. Up to 3 or 4 phones can listen at once.

data.name: ErrorOpenApp
data.value: Open the app to start sharing.

data.name: ErrorPermissionsBroadcast
data.value: AuraMusic needs Bluetooth, notifications and audio capture.

data.name: ErrorPairFirst
data.value: Pair the phones first in the Bluetooth settings.

data.name: UpdateMessage
data.value: AuraMusic {0} is available. Install it now?

data.name: UpdateAllowInstall
data.value: Allow AuraMusic to install apps, then restart the app to update.
